Bunraku design system taste

Taste

Every variant from every builder, on one page, on one theme switch. Pick a variant per item, leave a note, then export picks as JSON. Switch theme in the bar above to check a pick in G3, C1, C3 and paper.

  • Controls
  • HUD and cards
  • Feedback and protected
  • Front door and shell
  • Library and Scenes
  • Workbench and tools
  • Settings
  • Agent
  • Trash and history

Variant A

Flush plate

G3 as approved: a solid action fill, a hairline ghost, a tinted quiet fill, flat.

States

Variant B

Bracketed command

Primary is a small framed plate whose corner brackets light on hover and focus. Ghost is bracket-only: no boundary at rest, brackets mark it on hover and focus.

States

Variant C

Key-cap command

Every button carries its shortcut in a key cap at its left edge, like a game prompt.

New: needs approvalOnly Enter and Esc are confirmed shortcuts (g3-hud.html); the rest show the idea with placeholder caps.

Tooltips

HelpDot, title hovers

Parts: ui.tooltip, ui.tooltip.body

Variant A

Ink plate

A small ink plate opens on hover and focus. Hover or tab to the dots to see it.

Injection order: when prompts share a position, the lower number goes first. Save half a second after you stop typing. CtrlS still works, and still saves at once. Open (demo): rendered in flow rather than popped over, so it is not clipped by this page's scrolling demo box.
Variant B

Help line

The hint opens as a full-width line under the control, overlaying its own reserved row.

Injection order Injection order: when prompts share a position, the lower number goes first. Autosave Save half a second after you stop typing. CtrlS still works, and still saves at once. Open (demo) Open (demo): flows in its reserved row for the screenshot.

Swatches

SwatchRow, ColorPicker entry

Parts: ui.swatches, ui.swatches.swatch

Variant A

Squares

Square swatches; the chosen one carries a check mark, never color alone. Each swatch sets the tint trio through data-deck, never a deck token directly.

Variant B

Palette slots

Numbered slots; the selected one shows its hex value in mono underneath. The six house pastels are byte-identical in every theme including paper, so the value printed is true everywhere.

Help / Docs

User docs

Developer docs

User docs

Edit a piece

Open a piece on the Workbench, change it through the Grid or Steps view, and save your draft explicitly before you close the tab.

The short version

Editing happens on the Workbench. A piece opens there as its own tab, already filled in with whatever your import carried, or with the blank template you started from, and it stays a private draft until you save it.

The editor panels

A character's editor opens with a strip of platform tabs above the fields. The first, labeled Bunraku, is the full card with nothing hidden.

Saving, and what happens if you don't

Every editor requires a name before Save does anything. Save writes your whole draft, not just what changed, so fields you haven't touched round-trip byte-for-byte.

Connections

MCP servers

Programs this machine runs so their tools join Kit's belt. Every external tool asks at the Gate before it runs.

"weather-tools" was rejected: command must be an absolute path or a known launcher.

relay-toolsuvx --from git+https... relay-server 6 tool(s) env: RELAY_TOKEN
local-fsC:\tools\fs-mcp.exe not connected
Bunraku as a server

Point any MCP client at Bunraku's own belt: the library, catalogs and renderers. Your client asks before each tool runs.

claude mcp add bunraku -- bunraku mcp "C:\Users\you\Bunraku"

Remote access

Turn on remote access

Bunraku stays on your machine. A private, encrypted link lets your own devices reach it, with no router changes and no ports opened. You sign in to Tailscale once (free); we open that page for you.

Local network access

A no-account option: reach this studio from devices on the same network, with no Tailscale sign-in. Each device enters a connect code, and you approve it here before it gets in.

A no-account option: reach this studio from devices on the same network, with no Tailscale sign-in. Each device enters a connect code, and you approve it here before it gets in.

Settings

Carried / New: Carried in full: Appearance (theme and house-accent swatches), Models (list, add/edit form, key-never-returned note), Connections (MCP list with a rejected-server message, add/edit form, the Bunraku-as-server snippet), Studio (home app, Library first deck, publish targets, engine checkouts), Workbench (autosave, reopen, editor layout and mode, follow behavior), About (update check, studio folder, project links, Windows shortcuts, Restart/Quit/Reset with the armed confirm state). Security, Remote access and Updates each have many more states in their own soft wireframes (10, 11 and 14 respectively, mostly dialogs and connection phases) than BUILD-BRIEF’s row names individually; this page carries one representative pair of states per area (Security: on/off; Remote: off/connected; Updates: ready/progress) rather than the full dialog set, to keep the page buildable in this pass. Every remaining Security/Remote/Updates state (the recovery-word dialogs, Tailscale phases, rollback confirms, etc.) is NOT yet drawn here; flagging this gap rather than silently shipping partial coverage. Secrets and recovery words are protected.* and are not drawn on this page (none of the carried Security states reach a secret-revealing dialog). Phone width is covered by the page-wide Width switch, not repeated here.

History

Carried / New: Carried: the lorebook Changes pane (per-change diff, Revert/Undo/Restore), the scene Cast wing’s card-changed notice with its Back to version N line, and the Updates version timeline (variant B draws it as pips on a track with the selected version’s detail card; variant A keeps the plain log rows carried from Settings’ Updates tab). These three surfaces live in three different rooms in the real app (Workbench/lorebook editor, Scenes, Settings); this reference page shows them stacked with the Dock fixed on Workbench rather than rebuilding three separate shells, since BUILD-BRIEF states there is no standalone history browser to draw as its own room. Phone width is covered by the page-wide Width switch, not repeated here.
